title: Splanchnic Blood Volume by Cardiovascular MR as a Novel Marker of Haemodynamic Congestion across the Heart-Failure Spectrum: A Pilot Study
summary:
We aim to find out whether the abdominal blood volume (splanchnic blood volume, SBV) can serve as a new sign of fluid congestion in heart failure. We use a clinically indicated cardiac MRI with contrast and add a non-invasive SBV measurement during the same scan, about 5 additional minutes only. There are three groups: healthy controls, people with grade II diastolic dysfunction, and people with grade III/IV. We will compare SBV between groups and explore links with heart ultrasound measures, symptoms and functional status (e.g., NYHA class, blood pressure, BMI), and blood tests (e.g., NT-proBNP).
The study plans to enroll 24 participants (8 per group). It is non-interventional; no extra drugs or invasive procedures are required.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years 
Written informed consent
Scheduled for a clinically indicated contrast-enhanced cardiovascular MR that meets one of the three cohort definitions above
Exclusion criteria:
Standard MR contraindications (ferromagnetic implants, severe claustrophobia, etc.) 
Contraindication to gadolinium contrast (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² or prior severe allergic reaction)
Hemodynamic instability requiring inotropic support or mechanical heart assistance 
Inability to give informed consent
Pregnancy or lactation
Participation in another clinical trial with an investigational device or drug that could interfere with the outcomes
